idioms.meaning: to tell a secret by accident
idioms.example: Did you spill the beans?

idioms.meaning: to study hard
idioms.example: I need to hit the books before the exam.

idioms.meaning: an important matter
idioms.example: It's not a big deal, don't worry.

idioms.meaning: to try something, accepting the risk
idioms.example: Just give it a shot.

idioms.meaning: something very easy
idioms.example: The exam was a piece of cake.

idioms.meaning: to start a conversation with strangers
idioms.example: He told a joke to break the ice.

idioms.meaning: feeling slightly ill
idioms.example: I'm a bit under the weather today.

idioms.meaning: very rarely
idioms.example: We meet once in a blue moon.

idioms.en: cost an arm and a leg
idioms.meaning: to be very expensive
idioms.example: That car cost me an arm and a leg.

idioms.meaning: to become good at something after practice
idioms.example: You'll get the hang of it.

idioms.meaning: completely unexpected
idioms.example: He called me out of the blue.

idioms.meaning: to stop working for now
idioms.example: It's five — let's call it a day.

idioms.meaning: a bad event that turns out good
idioms.example: Losing that job was a blessing in disguise.

idioms.meaning: to do something unpleasant you cannot avoid
idioms.example: We'll have to bite the bullet.

idioms.meaning: to watch or look after
idioms.example: Keep an eye on my bag, please.

idioms.meaning: over the whole body
idioms.example: He was wet from head to toe.

idioms.meaning: the final problem that causes you to give up
idioms.example: That was the last straw.

idioms.meaning: alert and quick to react
idioms.example: She is always on the ball.

idioms.meaning: to become afraid and change your mind
idioms.example: He got cold feet before signing.

idioms.meaning: in the same difficult situation
idioms.example: We're all in the same boat.

idioms.meaning: to do something cheaply and badly
idioms.example: Don't cut corners on safety.

idioms.meaning: to be too late for an opportunity
idioms.example: Don't miss the boat — apply today.

idioms.meaning: some advice
idioms.example: Can I give you a piece of advice?

idioms.meaning: used to say something true, maybe surprising
idioms.example: To be honest, I disagree.

idioms.meaning: based on the information I have
idioms.example: As far as I know, the shop is open.

idioms.meaning: used to introduce the real point
idioms.example: The thing is, I have no money.

idioms.en: let the cat out of the bag
idioms.meaning: to reveal a secret
idioms.example: She let the cat out of the bag.

idioms.meaning: in trouble
idioms.example: He's in hot water with his teacher.

idioms.meaning: something fortunate
idioms.example: It was a piece of luck that we met.

idioms.meaning: being managed well
idioms.example: Everything is under control.

idioms.meaning: memorised
idioms.example: I know the poem by heart.

idioms.meaning: gradually, a little each day
idioms.example: He gets better day by day.

idioms.meaning: you must suffer to gain something
idioms.example: No pain, no gain — keep training.

idioms.meaning: things are going well until now
idioms.example: So far so good — half way there.

idioms.meaning: agreeing about the same plan or facts
idioms.example: Let's make sure we're on the same page before the meeting.

idioms.meaning: to start something so it can continue
idioms.example: I'll get the ball rolling and you can take over later.

idioms.meaning: keep me informed about what is happening
idioms.example: Please keep me in the loop about the new dates.

idioms.meaning: to talk briefly to check how things are
idioms.example: Let's touch base on Friday.

idioms.meaning: to learn how a job is done
idioms.example: It took me a month to learn the ropes.

idioms.meaning: to do your fair share of the work
idioms.example: Everyone has to pull their weight on this team.

idioms.meaning: to start planning again after a failure
idioms.example: The client said no, so it's back to the drawing board.

idioms.meaning: to do something badly to save time or money
idioms.example: They cut corners on testing and it showed.

idioms.meaning: to stop working for the day
idioms.example: It's already six — let's call it a day.

idioms.meaning: to accept something difficult and get it over with
idioms.example: I bit the bullet and asked for a raise.

idioms.meaning: to work late into the night
idioms.example: She burned the midnight oil to finish the report.

idioms.meaning: to take responsibility when it is needed
idioms.example: Someone has to step up and lead this.

idioms.meaning: planned and being worked on
idioms.example: Two new courses are in the pipeline.

idioms.meaning: a lot to learn quickly at the start
idioms.example: The new software had a steep learning curve.

idioms.meaning: delayed so something else can be done first
idioms.example: The redesign is on the back burner this month.

idioms.meaning: slightly ill or not yourself
idioms.example: I'm a bit under the weather today.

idioms.fa: از خوشحالی در پوست خود نگنجیدن
idioms.meaning: extremely happy
idioms.example: She was over the moon about the results.

idioms.meaning: sad and without energy
idioms.example: He's been down in the dumps since the exam.

idioms.meaning: very happy and excited
idioms.example: They were on cloud nine after the wedding.

idioms.meaning: nervous excitement before something big
idioms.example: I had butterflies in my stomach before the interview.

idioms.en: at the end of my rope
idioms.meaning: no strength left to keep trying
idioms.example: After three sleepless nights I was at the end of my rope.

idioms.meaning: annoyed because something has gone on too long
idioms.example: I'm fed up with the same excuses.

idioms.meaning: to release strong feelings safely
idioms.example: He goes running to blow off steam.

idioms.meaning: stay positive when things are hard
idioms.example: Keep your chin up — the worst is over.

idioms.fa: جا زدن / پشیمون شدن در لحظهٔ آخر
idioms.meaning: to become nervous and want to back out
idioms.example: He got cold feet the night before the move.

idioms.en: have a lot on my plate
idioms.meaning: to have a lot to deal with
idioms.example: I can't take anything else on — I've got a lot on my plate.

idioms.meaning: imagine my situation before judging
idioms.example: Put yourself in my shoes for a second.

idioms.meaning: good luck — said to someone about to perform. It is never a wish for an injury
idioms.example: Break a leg at the concert tonight!

idioms.meaning: hoping it works out
idioms.example: Fingers crossed the visa comes through.

idioms.meaning: greeting someone you have not seen in a while
idioms.example: Long time no see — how have you been?

idioms.meaning: to leave or start a journey
idioms.example: We should hit the road before the traffic builds.

idioms.meaning: to eat something quickly
idioms.example: Do you want to grab a bite after class?

idioms.meaning: help me with something physical or short
idioms.example: Give me a hand with these boxes.

idioms.meaning: wait a moment
idioms.example: Hang on, I'll check the address.

idioms.fa: آرام باش / خودت را ناراحت نکن
idioms.meaning: relax, or calm down
idioms.example: Take it easy — nobody is angry with you.

idioms.meaning: suddenly and without warning
idioms.example: She called me out of the blue last night.

idioms.meaning: very rarely
idioms.example: We eat out once in a blue moon.

idioms.meaning: said when the person you were discussing arrives
idioms.example: Speak of the devil — we were just talking about you!

idioms.fa: دیر رسیدن بهتر از هرگز نرسیدن
idioms.meaning: doing something late is still better than not doing it
idioms.example: He finally replied — better late than never.

idioms.meaning: things are going well up to now
idioms.example: We're on week four — so far so good.

idioms.meaning: that's fine; don't apologise
idioms.example: “Sorry for the delay.” “No worries.”

idioms.meaning: to stop for the night and go home or to bed
idioms.example: It's midnight — let's call it a night.
